- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after a spike; add 2–5% to forecast for that window.
- Model overestimates in the 20–30 day horizon after a spike; reduce forecast by 3–7% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.73 to -0.50), model often fails to adjust; apply a 3–5% downward correction to avoid lagged overreaction.
- Model tends to underestimate the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
